_description: Known lower bounds for the bilinear rank of small ⟨n,m,p⟩ matmul formats. Field-specific where known. 'tight: true' means a matching upper-bound algorithm exists in our catalog. Manually maintained — add entries as new lower bounds are published.

_schema.format: [n, m, p] — canonical (sorted) ordering, since rank is permutation-invariant
_schema.field: Which fields the lower bound is PROVEN over. Unlike upper bounds (a scheme over Z is automatically valid over Q/R/C/F2/F3 by inclusion + reduction), a lower bound does NOT inherit across fields: a char-0 floor does not transfer to F2/F3, and an F2 floor does not transfer to char-0. So name exactly what is proven. Tokens: a single field (F2 | F3 | R | C); a '/'-separated explicit set (e.g. 'F2/Z/Q/R/C' = proven over F2 and characteristic 0, but weaker/unknown over F3); 'char0' = the characteristic-0 fields Z/Q/R/C only (NOT F2/F3); 'all' = RESERVED for a genuinely field-agnostic ARGUMENT — one proof valid over arbitrary fields of any characteristic (e.g. Blaser's 'over arbitrary fields' rank families, or R(<2,2,2>)=7). Do NOT use 'all' merely because a value happens to coincide across the fields you checked — that over-claims; use an explicit set instead.
_schema.lb: lower bound on the bilinear rank
_schema.model: Which ALGEBRAIC MODEL the bound is proven in — the axis the 'field' token does NOT capture. 'bilinear' (the DEFAULT when the key is absent) = a floor on the non-commutative bilinear rank R; it constrains non-commutative claims ONLY, and says nothing about a commutative-only algorithm, since R_c ≤ R. 'quadratic' = a floor on the multiplicative complexity, i.e. proven even when the algorithm may exploit commutativity of the inputs; such a bound constrains BOTH models (R_c ≥ lb, hence R ≥ lb). Load-bearing: the catalog once carried a commutative R_c(<2,2,2>)=6 claim under the very papers that forbid it — the refutation was in this file all along, but nothing could tell that Winograd's floor also binds the commutative axis. Only tag 'quadratic' when the source proves it in that model; do NOT infer it from a value coinciding across models.
_schema.tight: whether some algorithm achieves this rank (some entry in catalog.json matches lb)
_schema.source: primary reference (citation key — use the SAME string across multiple entries for the same paper, so the reference registry deduplicates correctly)
_schema.notes: anything else worth surfacing (e.g., which formula was applied)

entries.notes: Classical: rank exactly 7 in any field. Independently proven by Hopcroft & Kerr (Cornell TR 69-44, Sep 1969 / SIAM 1971) and Winograd (in the same 1971 paper that introduces the Winograd-Strassen 15-additions variant). Later re-proven by Pan 1980. Matches Strassen 1969. MODEL (2026-08-30): 'quadratic' — Hopcroft–Kerr proved 7 minimal WITHOUT commutativity; Winograd's note (abstract: 'the minimum number of multiplications required to multiply two 2 x 2 matrices is seven', intro: the point is to show it 'using the commutativity law') extends the floor to the commutative model, so R_c(⟨2,2,2⟩) = 7 too — commutativity buys nothing at size 2.

Tight over F₂ (confirmed by Wang 2026 arXiv:2603.07280, table) and over characteristic 0; matches Smirnov / Hopcroft-Kerr construction. Also independently established by Alexeev 1985 (J.Algorithms 6, 71–85), cited as [6] in Burichenko 2014 (arXiv:1408.6273). NARROWED from 'all' (2026-06-26): over F₃ only ≥10 is known (Bläser 1999, reproduced by Wang 2026) — see the separate F₃ entry; the tight 11 is NOT established over F₃.

Formula R(⟨2,2,n⟩) = ⌈7n/2⌉ for n ≥ 2 (Hopcroft–Kerr tight). Also established by Alexeev–Smirnov 2013, 'On exact and approximate complexities of multiplication of matrices of sizes 4×2 and 2×2', Contemporary problems of mathematics 17, 135–152 (in Russian), cited as [7] in Burichenko 2014 (arXiv:1408.6273). NARROWED from 'all' (2026-06-26): tight over F₂ (Hopcroft–Kerr per Wang 2026) and over characteristic 0 (Alexeev–Smirnov); the value over F₃ is unconfirmed, so 'all' (a field-agnostic claim) was unjustified.

Formula R(⟨2,2,n⟩) = ⌈7n/2⌉ for n ≥ 2. NARROWED from 'all' (2026-06-26): tight over F₂ (Hopcroft–Kerr per Wang 2026) and over characteristic 0; the value over F₃ is unconfirmed, so 'all' was unjustified.

Hopcroft–Kerr 1971, Theorem 1 + abstract: the ⌈(3pn+max(n,p))/2⌉ construction is proven minimal for p=1 or 2 (any n) and for p=3, n=3. The p=3, n=3 case = ⟨3,2,3⟩ = ⟨2,3,3⟩ by S₃ symmetry → R(⟨2,3,3⟩) = 15 tight. Also proven by Pan 1978. (Burichenko 2014 [arXiv:1408.6273] cites only Bläser 2003's weaker LB≥14 as ref [9], but the HK proof of minimality for p=3,n=3 is explicit and pre-dates Bläser by 32 years.) Confirmed over F₂ by Wang 2026 (arXiv:2603.07280, table). NARROWED from 'all' (2026-06-26): over F₃ only ≥14 is known (Bläser 1999, reproduced by Wang 2026) — see the separate F₃ entry; the tight 15 is NOT established over F₃.

Tight over characteristic 0 (Z/Q/R/C): UB 20 is Smirnov's construction, matched from below. NARROWED from 'all' (2026-06-26): the lower bound of 20 does NOT hold over F₂ — a char-0 LB does not transfer to characteristic 2. Wang 2026 (arXiv:2603.07280, Thm 2) proves only R_{F₂}(⟨2,3,4⟩) ≥ 19 with UB 20, so over F₂ the format is open in [19,20]. See the separate Wang F₂ entry.

Bläser, M. 'On the complexity of the multiplication of matrices of small formats', J.Complexity 19, 43–60. Applies over R, C, Q. Best upper bound is 23 (Laderman 1976) — gap of 4 remains open. Held the SOTA for ⟨3,3,3⟩ since 2003. WIDENED from 'R'/'C' to 'all' (2026-06-26) and merged with the former separate C entry: per Wang 2026 (arXiv:2603.07280) §1.1, Bläser's R(⟨n,m,n⟩) ≥ 2mn+2n−m−2 (m≥n≥3) holds over ARBITRARY fields, so ⟨3,3,3⟩ ≥ 19 is field-agnostic (incl. Z/Q/R/C/F2/F3). SUPERSEDED over F₂ by Wang 2026 (≥20, Theorem 1) — see the separate F₂ entry; the 19 floor still stands over F₃ and characteristic 0.

Wang, C. 'Automated Lower Bounds for Small Matrix Multiplication Complexity over Finite Fields', arXiv:2603.07280 (Mar 2026, latest revision May 2026). Theorem 1. Strengthens Bläser's 19 specifically over F₂ using orbit classification + dynamic programming with verifiable proof certificates. UB still 23; gap of 3. The R/C/Q bound is unchanged at 19 — extending Wang's method to characteristic 0 is open.

Wang 2026 (arXiv:2603.07280), Theorem 2: R_{F₂}(⟨2,3,4⟩) ≥ 19. Completes a proof that Hopcroft–Kerr 1971 [9] stated but omitted. Previous F₂ LB was 18 (Bläser 1999 [2]). UB 20 (Hopcroft–Kerr); gap of 1 — over F₂ the format is open in [19,20]. (Over characteristic 0 the format is tight at 20 — see the Smirnov 2013 char0 entry.)
Wang 2026 (arXiv:2603.07280), Theorem 3: R_{F₂}(⟨3,3,4⟩) ≥ 25. Improves the previous F₂ LB of 24 (Bläser 2003 [3]). UB 29 (Smirnov 2013 [13]); gap of 4.
Wang 2026 (arXiv:2603.07280), Theorem 4: R_{F₂}(⟨3,4,4⟩) ≥ 29. Improves the previous F₂ LB of 28 (Bläser 1999 [2]). UB 38 (Smirnov 2013 [13]); gap of 9.

Bläser, M. 'Lower bounds for the multiplicative complexity of matrix multiplication', computational complexity 8(3):203–226, 1999 (ref [2] in Wang 2026). R_{F₃}(⟨2,2,2⟩) ≥ 7; tight (Strassen UB 7). Reproduced over F₃ by Wang 2026's automated framework — attribution_for_rank: Bläser 1999, NOT Wang (a re-derivation, not a discovery).

Bläser 1999 (computational complexity 8(3), ref [2] in Wang 2026): R_{F₃}(⟨2,2,3⟩) ≥ 10. Reproduced over F₃ by Wang 2026's automated framework — attribution_for_rank: Bläser 1999, not Wang. (Over F₂ the same format is tight at 11.)

Bläser 1999 (computational complexity 8(3), ref [2] in Wang 2026): R_{F₃}(⟨2,3,3⟩) ≥ 14. Reproduced over F₃ by Wang 2026's automated framework — attribution_for_rank: Bläser 1999, not Wang. (Over F₂ / char 0 the same format is tight at 15.)
UB: 49 (Strassen²), 48 over C (AlphaEvolve 2025), 47 over F₂ (AlphaTensor 2022).
Border-rank-based argument. UB: 93 (AlphaEvolve 2025); gap remains large.

R(⟨5,5,5⟩) ≥ 2·5·5 + 2·5 − 5 − 2 = 53, via Bläser's R(⟨n,m,n⟩) ≥ 2mn+2n−m−2 (m≥n≥3) over ARBITRARY fields (Bläser 2003, J.Complexity 19, 43–60 = ref [3] in Wang 2026 §1.1; the same formula yields ⟨3,3,3⟩≥19). STRENGTHENED 2026-06-26 from the weaker 48 = ⌈(5/2)·5²−3·5⌉ (Bläser via Landsberg 2008, Bull.AMS 45(2):247–284, Thm 3.8.4); for n≤7 the 2n²+n−2 formula dominates 5/2·n²−3n, for n≥8 vice-versa. Not tight: UB 93 (AlphaEvolve 2025).

R(⟨6,6,6⟩) ≥ 2·6·6 + 2·6 − 6 − 2 = 76, via Bläser's R(⟨n,m,n⟩) ≥ 2mn+2n−m−2 (m≥n≥3) over ARBITRARY fields (Bläser 2003, J.Complexity 19, 43–60 = ref [3] in Wang 2026 §1.1). STRENGTHENED 2026-06-26 from the weaker 72 = ⌈(5/2)·6²−3·6⌉ (Bläser via Landsberg 2008, Bull.AMS 45(2):247–284, Thm 3.8.4). Not tight: UBs are ~m^2.37 vs Θ(m²).

R(⟨7,7,7⟩) ≥ 2·7·7 + 2·7 − 7 − 2 = 103, via Bläser's R(⟨n,m,n⟩) ≥ 2mn+2n−m−2 (m≥n≥3) over ARBITRARY fields (Bläser 2003, J.Complexity 19, 43–60 = ref [3] in Wang 2026 §1.1). STRENGTHENED 2026-06-26 from the weaker 102 = ⌈(5/2)·7²−3·7⌉ (Bläser via Landsberg 2008, Bull.AMS 45(2):247–284, Thm 3.8.4); 103 is the last n where 2n²+n−2 beats 5/2·n²−3n (n≥8 reverts). Not tight: UBs are ~m^2.37 vs Θ(m²).

R̃(⟨2,2,2⟩) = 7 (border rank). Closed a 23-year open question — Bini 1980 introduced border rank, Strassen 1983 proved R̃ ≥ 6, but whether the border-rank could improve on the tensor rank of 7 was open until Landsberg 2006 settled R̃ = 7 exactly. Implication: no ε-aggregation trick can multiply 2×2 matrices with fewer than 7 bilinear multiplications. NARROWED from 'all' (2026-06-26): border rank was settled over C (algebraically closed, characteristic 0) by Landsberg's geometric argument — it is not a characteristic-free result, so 'all' was unjustified.
